title: Vessel Stress Mapping and Preventive Stroke-Risk Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (VSM-ULM)
description: This project builds on recent advances in ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM/sULM) to treat stroke as a mechanical fatigue problem of the microvasculature. Using contrast microbubbles as Lagrangian tracers, we reconstruct the microvascular network and compute vessel-level stress and fragility metrics (Vessel Stress Index, Network Fragility Score) from track-derived features such as velocity, recirculation, normalized distance, and dwell time. To make ULM clinically trustworthy, we propose a Birth-Time Cone Ledger: a physically-constrained, audit-ready multi-object tracker that maintains per-bubble identity with organ-specific speed/acceleration priors and explicit quality flags ("clean / suspicious / broken" trajectories). On the sensing side, we outline a stress-reporting tracer concept: a second-layer contrast agent (shear- or inflammation-responsive) that irreversibly changes its US/PA signal in mechanically or biochemically stressed segments. Its per-segment signal (SRI) is fused with the ULM-derived stress metrics into a Composite Risk Index for each vessel. Finally, we specify a cheap, CEUS-based clinical workflow that runs on existing high-end ultrasound systems, with realistic scan times, GPU-accelerated processing, coverage/QC reporting, and simple outputs (heatmaps + scores) suitable for preventive screening and follow-up in high-risk patients. What is new compared to current research – We turn ULM track data into an explicit microvascular fatigue geometry (VSI + NFS), rather than only mapping perfusion or velocity. – We introduce a physically-gated tracking ledger tailored for clinical auditability, complementary to existing Kalman/GLMB/LSTM tracking schemes. – We frame stress-responsive contrast as a diagnostic, repeatable "risk paint" layer on top of CEUS, instead of purely theranostic nanoparticles. – We design a full, low-cost stroke-risk exam that could realistically be implemented on current CEUS equipment, rather than a single algorithm or phantom study.

title: Genetic association between sleep quality, insomnia, and psychological distress: systematic review and meta-analysis
description: The relationship between poor sleep quality and psychological distress has been shown in several studies and meta-analyses (Dalcalı et al., 2021; Gregory et al., 2011; Kim et al., 2022; Madrid-Valero et al., 2020). Genetic factors explain a large proportion of individual differences in these variables, and both Twin Studies and Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) have shown a significant genetic overlap between them. However, this overlap varies widely across studies, and the factors that explain this heterogeneity are still not completely understood. This meta-analysis aims to: 1) estimate the mean genetic correlation between sleep problems and psychological distress; 2) assess heterogeneity among the included studies; and 3) search for possible moderators that could contribute to this heterogeneity. title: Association Between Incretin-Based Therapies and Ocular Outcomes in Adults: A Systematic Review with Qualitative Synthesis
description: This study is a systematic review designed to identify, synthesize, and characterize the available evidence on the association between incretin-based therapies and ocular health outcomes in adult populations. Incretin-based therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonists, are widely used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. While their metabolic and cardiovascular benefits are well established, emerging evidence has raised questions regarding their potential effects on ocular health, including diabetic retinopathy, macular disease, optic neuropathy, glaucoma, and other visual outcomes. The available literature is highly heterogeneous, encompassing randomized controlled trials, observational studies, post hoc analyses, registry-based data, and pharmacovigilance reports. Ocular outcomes are frequently reported as secondary or exploratory endpoints, with substantial variability in definitions, measurement methods, and reporting standards. Additionally, findings across studies are often inconsistent, with reports suggesting potential beneficial, neutral, or adverse associations depending on the specific agent, population characteristics, and study design. The primary objective of this review is to systematically synthesize the evidence on the association between incretin-based therapies and ocular outcomes, with a focus on characterizing the direction and nature of reported associations across different study designs and clinical contexts. Secondary objectives include identifying which ocular outcomes have been evaluated, examining how these outcomes are defined and measured, comparing findings across different incretin-based agents, and identifying key methodological limitations and knowledge gaps in the current literature. This review includes randomized and non-randomized studies conducted in adult populations receiving incretin-based therapies for any clinical indication. A comprehensive literature search was performed in MEDLINE (via PubMed) and Embase from database inception to February 2026. Study selection and data extraction were conducted independently by two reviewers using predefined eligibility criteria and standardized extraction frameworks. Screening and data extraction processes were supported by a structured, rule-based computational system within a human-in-the-loop framework, with all decisions validated by reviewers. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, outcome definitions, and reporting approaches, no quantitative meta-analysis was performed. Instead, findings are synthesized using structured qualitative (narrative) methods, incorporating classification of the direction of association, characterization of evidence sources, and comparative analysis across therapies and outcome domains. A formal risk of bias assessment was not conducted, as the primary aim of the review is to characterize the breadth, patterns, and consistency of the available evidence rather than to estimate pooled effect sizes or establish causal inference. The expected outcomes of this review include a comprehensive mapping and synthesis of the evidence on ocular outcomes associated with incretin-based therapies, identification of consistent and inconsistent patterns across studies, and delineation of key gaps in the literature. The findings are intended to inform clinical interpretation, guide interdisciplinary collaboration between endocrinology and ophthalmology, and support future research and evidence-based recommendations in this area.

title: Ocularity Singleton and Statistical Learning in Virtual Reality
description: This project investigates whether statistical learning of distractor locations can occur when the distractor is defined by monocular saliency—a property that is invisible to participants' conscious perception but salient at the level of early visual cortex (V1). The study builds on the concept of Ocularity Singletons, stimuli that are selectively visible to only one eye and are known to activate monocular neurons in V1. Although these stimuli are perceptually indistinguishable from other stimuli to the participant, their unique monocular input gives them higher bottom-up salience (Zhaoping, 2008b, 2008a, 2012). As a result, they can act as unintentional distractors, capturing attention covertly. Statistical learning refers to the brain's ability to extract regularities from the environment through repeated exposure, without explicit instruction or conscious awareness. In the domain of visual attention, statistical learning enables observers to implicitly suppress spatial locations based on the learned likelihood of salient distractor appearance (Duncan et al., 2023; Wang & Theeuwes, 2018). In this study, we want to examine two research questions: 1. Is conscious perception of salience necessary for statistical learning to occur? By using a distractor that is perceptually equivalent to others, yet neurally more salient, we can test whether statistical learning mechanisms require awareness of salience, or whether they can operate purely at an implicit level. 2. Does statistical learning operate at the level of spatial regularities, or is it constrained by the specific sensory pathways through which stimuli are processed? To address these questions, we adapt a statistical learning paradigm into a virtual reality (VR) setting, incorporating Ocularity Singletons as distractors. This novel combination allows us to probe the interaction between early visual salience and statistical learning. Ultimately, this research aims to shed light on how attention and learning mechanisms operate under conditions where salience is defined at the earliest stages of visual processing, and whether implicit learning can adapt to such bottom-up biases. title: A Dual-Layered Structure of Reality
description: This manuscript develops a dual-layered metaphysical framework, grounded in information theory and thermodynamics, to reconcile determinism with informational agency. It posits a structural stratification of reality into a deterministic lattice of potential (L1) and a finite layer of realization (I2), where agency emerges via structural compression reframing the epistemic veil as a constitutive necessity. The framework is justified by the External Reference Paradox (ERP), which employs continuous-time models and deductive arguments to demonstrate that single-layer matter-first ontologies constitute finite, informationally closed systems lacking a stable external reference for long-term error correction and are therefore structurally collapse-bound. This logical limitation is compounded by thermodynamic and dimensional deficits: closed single-layer models lack an entropy sink capable of sustaining biological and informational complexity against the Second Law, and fail to distinguish the static lattice of potential from the sequential traversal of realization. These failures are formalized through boundary conditions that distinguish thermodynamic Totality from Subsystem behavior and establish Asymmetric Persistence as the requisite test for structural viability. The dual-layered framework is therefore proposed as the structural minimum necessary to satisfy both the logical requirements for error correction and the physical requirements of an open, evolving system. Continuity is defined by conservation of information across layers rather than conservation of matter. Reality is derived as R = P(L1) ∙ N(I2), unfolding through realignment, a process by which the informational layer instantiates finite life-paths from the deterministic lattice. Constrained by informational finitude, this structure yields a Finite-Worlds framework in which agents occupy limited branches per epoch, in contrast to unrestricted multiverse interpretations. Quantum probability is reinterpreted as the geometric density of pre-encoded trajectories within the lattice. Ultimately, agency is framed not as a violation of determinism, but as the evolutionary capacity of information to navigate an exhaustive space of possibilities. Quantum theory is treated as an interpretive and modeling lens that complements this ontology, which describes reality independently of any specific microphysical formulation.

title: Risk factors of age-related macular degeneration. A meta-review.
description: A meta-review, also known as an overview of systematic review, reviews of reviews, or umbrella review, is defined as the use explicit and systematic methods to search for and identify multiple systematic reviews on related research questions in the same topic area for the purpose of extracting and analysing their results across important outcomes. The primary reason for conducting meta-reviews is to address research questions that are broader in scope than those examined in individual systematic reviews. Other reasons include time and resource savings, as meta-review can be conducted more quickly than conventional systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and the need to understand the diversity present in the existing systematic review literature. Some meta-reviews have revealed important and comprehensive findings on dry eye interventions and adverse events associated with anti–vascular endothelial growth factor treatments. This consolidated evidence provides healthcare practitioners with greater confidence in applying these treatments in clinical practice. Therefore, this meta-review aimed to synthesize the evidence from published systematic reviews on non-pharmacological, risk factors for preventing and delaying AMD.

title: Current evidence of PET-Guided Biopsy in Head and Neck Lesions: A Systematic Review
description: This research project is a systematic review conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines, aiming to comprehensively evaluate the role of PET-guided percutaneous biopsy in the diagnosis and management of head and neck lesions, including deep-seated tumors and complex cervical nodal disease. The project synthesizes available literature from 2000 to mid-2025, focusing on studies in which positron-emission tomography (PET), fused with ultrasound (US), CT, or cone-beam CT (CBCT), was actively used to guide biopsy needle placement. Purpose: The primary objective of the project is to determine whether PET-guided biopsy provides a diagnostic and clinical advantage over traditional methods like US- or CT-guided fine-needle aspiration (FNA) or core needle biopsy (CNB), particularly in challenging anatomical regions such as the skull base, parapharyngeal space, and infratemporal fossa. Given the limitations of conventional imaging in detecting viable tumor tissue in these regions—owing to necrosis, fibrosis, or difficult access—this review explores how metabolic navigation using PET tracers (primarily FDG) can improve target selection, sampling adequacy, and ultimately, treatment planning. Key Components of the Study: Systematic search across major databases and grey literature using a pre-registered protocol. Inclusion criteria focused on prospective or retrospective cohort studies with ≥5 patients undergoing PET-guided FNA or CNB. Extraction of data on technical parameters, navigation platforms, tracer types, complication rates, diagnostic adequacy, sensitivity/specificity, and changes in downstream management. Findings and Expected Outcomes: PET-guided biopsy demonstrated high sample adequacy (94–100%) and sensitivity (up to 100%), even in deep-seated or necrotic lesions. It showed significant clinical impact, altering treatment plans in over 80% of patients—by avoiding unnecessary surgery, expediting chemoradiation, or identifying occult metastases. Complication rates were minimal, with no reported cases of cranial nerve injury or tumor seeding. Fusion platforms combining PET with real-time US or optical navigation proved especially effective in expanding access to previously "blind" anatomical zones. Emerging modalities like FAPI-PET and PSMA-PET, as well as technologies such as AI-driven path planning and robotic needle systems, suggest a promising future for precision-targeted interventions. Significance: This project underscores the evolving role of PET-directed image-guided biopsy as a minimally invasive, high-yield alternative to open surgical biopsy in complex head and neck cases. The findings advocate for broader adoption of hybrid navigation workflows, encourage investment in training and infrastructure, and call for multi-institutional prospective studies to further validate clinical and cost outcomes. By consolidating and critically appraising the available data, this review helps clinicians, radiologists, and surgeons make informed decisions about incorporating PET-guided techniques into routine diagnostic pathways—especially in equivocal, recurrent, or surgically inaccessible disease.

title: Word Formation of Photography Terminologies
description: Technology and social media affected the use of word as part of language in certain domain as a means of communication. The research objectives were to find out the types of word formation, the dominant type and the reason of dominancy of word formation of photography terminologies in online magazine outdoorphotographer.com. It was a descriptive qualitative research concerning on exploring language particularly on word level. Data were collected from articles published on online magazine from January to August 2018 by reading, note-taking and check-listing. To analyze the types of word formation, a theory by Stockwell and Minkova was used and to analyze the meaning of the terminologies, Cambridge and Oxford dictionaries were used. The result showed that there were 198 photography terminologies found. These terminologies were classified into six types of word formation, namely acronym (12 data), borrowing (3 data), compounding (166 data), clipping (3 data), derivation (3 data) and eponym (1 datum). The most dominant type was compounding. It was very dominant due to its simplicity to form a new word by simply combining two or more words without any change of its elements. This research revealed many photography terminologies that could be used to enrich vocabulary.

description: Objetive: The purpose of this study is to conduct a systematic review in order to identify and critically analyse the best available evidence concerning the effects of physical exercise training programmes on IOP in people with Glaucoma. Methods: It conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) Search strategy: Three electronic databases (MEDLINE/Web of Science, PubMed and Scopus) were searched systematically from their inception until April 2023 by combining the keywords "Glaucoma" AND "exercise". Eligibility criteria Investigations that provided information regarding the effects of physical exercise on the IOP of people with glaucoma were considered eligible. Investigations were excluded if: a) data came from a case study; b) the intervention was based on yoga performance; c) exercise was performed in combination with other therapies; d) the sample included both healthy people and patients with glaucoma and data was not provided separately for each group; e) IOP was not an outcome of interest; f) the full-text of the study was not available; and g) the research was not written in English, Portuguese or Spanish language.

title: Supplemental materials for preprint: Effectiveness of a smartphone-based, augmented reality exposure app to reduce fear of spiders in real-life: a randomized controlled trial
description: Although in vivo exposure therapy is highly effective in the treatment of specific phobias, only a minority of patients seeks therapy. Exposure to virtual objects has been shown to be better tolerated, equally efficacious, but the technology has not been made widely accessible yet. We developed an augmented reality (AR) application (app) to reduce fear of spiders and performed a randomized controlled trial comparing the effects of our app (six 30-min sessions at home over a two-week period) with no intervention. Primary outcome was subjective fear, measured by a Subjective Units of Distress Scale (SUDS) in a Behavioural Approach Test (BAT) in a real-life spider situation at six weeks follow-up. Between Oct 7, 2019, and Dec 6, 2019, 66 individuals were enrolled and randomized. The intervention led to significantly lower subjective fear in the BAT compared to the control group (intervention group, baseline: 7·12 [SD 2·03] follow-up: 5·03 [SD 2·19] vs. control group, baseline: 7·06 [SD 2·34], follow-up 6·24 [SD 2.21]; adjusted group difference -1·24, 95% CI -2·17 to -0·31; Cohen's d=0·57, p=0·01). The repeated use of the AR app reduces subjective fear in a real-life spider situation, providing a low-threshold and low-cost treatment for fear of spiders.

title: Arctic Horizon Scan - OUPF
description: DOCUMENT IN REVIEW. In 2022, the Oxford University Polar Forum organised a horizon scanning exercise, aiming to identify Arctic research priorities for the next decade. First, a multilingual online survey ran for six months and invited contributions from researchers of all disciplines, people from local and Indigenous Arctic communities, policymakers, funders of research, and all other stakeholders. Next, >100 delegates distilled the online submissions into a categorised set of Arctic research priorities during a hybrid format workshop (in-situ and online) based in Oxford (United Kingdom), over 7-9 September 2022. The resulting document consists of 57 priority research questions. Each priority is presented as a statement/question, followed by three sections: knowledge gaps, methodologies, and examples. A glossary defines and/or contextualises >300 terms to widen access and readership. The delegates agreed that co-production of knowledge with Indigenous Peoples and convergent research approaches should be the norm in addressing research priorities in the Arctic. The document is currently under review.

title: Determinants of adherence to treatment in patients with ophthalmic conditions
description: Medications' adherence to ophthalmic drugs among patients with ophthalmic conditions can improve their clinical outcomes, quality of life and reduce healthcare costs. The objective of the study was to identify and determine factors associated with patients' ophthalmic medication adherence. Methods: After an exploratory analysis, logistic regression (LR) methods were used. The dataset (n=1144 patients) collected records from randomized clinical trials (RCTs) phase I-IV. Variables were ranked based on their significance to adherence levels using the LR variable importance methods. The stepwise elimination method was performed to obtain the explicatory adherence (≥ 80%) using the identified significance variables. LR models were developed with bootstrap to validate the model using the identified significance variables.

title: ophthalmic care nursing
description: Ophthalmic care in nursing is undeniably vital for preserving and enhancing the visual health of patients, averting vision impairment, and contributing significantly to their overall well-being. The eyes are often referred to as the windows to the soul, and provide a vital connection to the world around us. Nursing professionals specializing in ophthalmic care are entrusted with the responsibility of safeguarding and enhancing this precious sense. Nurses specializing in ophthalmology are at the forefront of preventing, diagnosing, and treating a wide range of eye conditions, from common refractive errors to complex ophthalmic disorders. Visual impairments and eye diseases can significantly impact an individual's quality of life, independence, and overall health. Ophthalmic care within the nursing profession encompasses a spectrum of preventive, educational, and supportive measures, aiming to comprehensively address issues related to eye health. ophthalmic care is not typically integrated into standard nursing curricula. Instead, it often appears as an elective component within undergraduate programs or post-graduate specialization. However, In this era of evolving healthcare, roles of nurses are expanding in various specialized and tertiary healthcare facilities, where ophthalmic care is a critical component, are generating an escalating demand for specialized training to adequately prepare nursing professionals. Formal, comprehensive advanced ophthalmic care training presents several notable advantages for nurses. It instills confidence and competence, directly translating into enhanced patient care and expanded career opportunities, ultimately contributing to personal and professional fulfillment. Furthermore, it equips nurses with the precise expertise required to deliver top-tier care within the specialized domain of eye health. In contrast, on-the-job learning or informal work-based education may prove time-consuming, lack structured content, and lack uniformity depending on the instructor and clinical setting. Such skills acquired in this manner may risk being non-transferrable to other ophthalmic contexts. It is imperative to examine existing ophthalmic care nursing curricula and identify the essential skills deemed necessary for specialized ophthalmic care nurses. This exploration aims to meet the growing demand for highly trained professionals in this field, ensuring that patients receive the best possible care while nurturing the growth of specialized nursing expertise in ophthalmic care.

title: Trace Source Emergent Origin of Culture Theory (TSI-OCT): Function → Requisites → Deficit → Behavior → Culture
description: TSI-OCT (Trace Source Emergent Origin of Culture Theory) proposes a trace-source, emergent evolutionary ontology for cultural origins framed as a sequential function-to-requisites-to-deficit-to-behavior-to-culture progression. In this account, once structure-and-function stabilizes, continuation becomes conditional on requisites; requisites imply the likelihood of shortfall; and shortfall, when present, is deficit. Deficit instantiates Need Functions (NF) as organized closure patterns that bias sensing, prioritization, coordination, and action toward restoring or advancing viable continuation within a declared boundary and horizon. Because closure is frequently complementary—distributed across internal and external co-mechanisms—effective closure often requires recruitment and coordinated participation at group scale. Communication is treated as a downstream instrument of recruitment rather than an origin cause: internal states and reasons are conveyed outward into a shared field so coordinated closure becomes feasible. Culture is defined as transmissible procedure-memory for repeated group closure across time (tools, roles, norms, routines, institutions).

title: SARS-CoV-2 detection by a clinical diagnostic RT-LAMP assay
description: The ongoing pandemic of SARS-CoV-2 calls for rapid and cost-effective methods to accurately identify infected individuals. The vast majority of patient samples is assessed for viral RNA presence by RT-qPCR. Our biomedical research institute, in collaboration between partner hospitals and an accredited clinical diagnostic laboratory, established a diagnostic testing pipeline that has reported on more than 252,000 RT-qPCR results since its commencement at the beginning of April 2020. title: The Effects of Hyper-Palatable Foods on Energy Intake Measured using Mobile Food Photography Methodology
description: ABSTRACT Objective Hyper-palatable foods (HPF) are designed with combinations of nutrients that serve to maximize their rewarding effects during consumption. Due to their artificially rewarding properties, HPF are hypothesized to lead to greater energy intake within a meal. However, this premise has not been tested in free living conditions. The current study examined the effects of HPF on 1) measured energy intake and 2) self-reported overeating, assessed within eating occasions using smartphone-based food photography methodology. Method A total of 29 participants reported food intake and eating experiences (N = 372) in real-time for 4 days using smartphone-based food photography methodology. HPF were identified using a standardized definition. Bayesian multilevel modeling was conducted to investigate the within-person effects of proportional calorie intake from HPF (%kcal HPF) on total energy intake and subjective overeating within eating occasions. Pre-meal hunger and proportional energy intake from high energy dense foods were included as covariates in the models. Results Results from Bayesian multi-level modeling revealed that when participants consumed more %kcal HPF during eating occasions relative to their average, they consumed greater total energy (median β = 0.09, 95% HDI [0.02, 0.16], pd = 99.62%). There was a >99% probability of positive association between %kcal HPF and total energy intake within an eating occasion. Additionally, the results suggested that when participants consumed more %kcal HPF during eating occasions relative to their average, participants endorsed higher eating more than planned (median β = 0.11, 95% HDI [-0.02, 0.25], pd = 95.74%) and eating despite feeling full (median β = 0.09, 95% HDI [-0.04, 0.23], pd = 91.02%). Conclusions The findings supported the premise that HPF themselves may yield greater energy intake and eating despite satiety, measured in real-time and free living conditions.

title: Comparison of the safety of outpatient cervical disc replacement with inpatient cervical disc replacement: a protocol for a meta-analysis
description: With the aging of the population and the change of lifestyle, the prevalence of cervical degenerative disc disease is increasing. Severe cases that cause radiculopathy or myelopathy require surgery to decompress the nerve and spinal cord and relief the symptom. Cervical disc replacement (CDR) is a relatively new technique to treat cervical degenerative disc disease and has been applied to clinical practice for twenty years. Compared with the traditional fusion surgery, CDR aims at preserving the range of motion at the pathological level and restoring the physiological properties of the cervical spine to the most extent. Several randomized controlled trials comparing the safety and efficiency of CDR with anterior cervical discectomy and fusion have proven the noninferiority of CDR. In addition, studies showed that both 1-level and 2-level CDR is more cost-effective in long-term follow-up. Therefore, CDR has been widely used in recent years. Although CDR is efficient in treating cervical degenerative disc disease, the cost of this procedure is very high. Saifi et al. reported that the mean hospital cost for CDR was $13,197 between 2005 and 2013. Kumar et al. used the MarketScan database and found that the mean cost of CDR was $28,664. Therefore, CDR may bring a great economic burden to patients and the health care system. Recently, with the advances in surgical techniques, anesthesiology, and perioperative care, many surgeries have been transited to outpatient procedures. The convenience of recovering at home rather than in hospital can generally shorten the recovery time and reduce the patient's stress. The outpatient surgery does not need an overnight hospital stay; hence it can keep the hospital-related cost down and save the patient's time. It is reported that outpatient procedures can reduce nearly 30% of the costs associated with hospitalization compared with inpatient procedures. Therefore, outpatient CDR could be used as a strategy to reduce costs. The number of outpatient CDR procedures shows an increasing trend in recent years. Several studies have reported the noninferiority of outpatient CDR compared with outpatient ACDF or inpatient CDR. However, the generalizability of these studies is limited by the retrospective study design, small sample size, and low incidence of CDR-associated complications. Therefore, the safety profile surrounding outpatient CDR remains poorly resolved. To evaluate the current evidence on the safety of outpatient CDR, we aim to perform a meta-analysis of the published studies. We hope our study will help surgeons fully understand the complications and safety profile surrounding outpatient CDR, and help improve the performance of outpatient CDR.

title: Present Bias, Self-Control, and Diabetes Self-Care
description: More than 38 million people in the U.S. have diabetes, which is associated with very serious health complications such as retinopathy, chronic kidney disease, and amputations. To improve the prognosis of individuals with diabetes, it is important to understand the psychological factors that might influence diabetes self-care. The demands of diabetes self-care can be overwhelming due to the sustained attention that is required. The present study is based on the behavior change model which asserts that while behavior change can be difficult, there are a multitude of strategies that can be implemented to support behavior change (Duckworth & Gross, 2020). Making good self-care decisions--and doing so consistently--requires willpower and strong behavioral control. Those who do not have such willpower succumb to the present bias, which reflects favoring short- over long-term rewards. In our upcoming research, we will conduct an anonymous online survey that will allow us to assess relationships between various psychosocial constructs and behavioral self-care. Importantly, it will also assess the psychometric characteristics of these measures.

title: Evaluation of head movement, pain sensitivity, and kinesiophobia in Patients with Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
description: Background and aim: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (IIH) is a rare headache disorder characterized by elevated intracranial pressure. Its incidence has doubled over the past decade in parallel with the global obesity epidemic (1). IIH affects about 85% women compared to men (2) and predominantly overweight and obese women of reproductive age, with an incidence of 20 per 100,000 compared to 0.5–2 per 100,000 in the general population (3). The clinical presentation is highly variable, and can include headache, tinnitus, nausea, visual disturbances, dizziness, fatigue, cognitive difficulties, and 42% of patients experience neck pain (4). Despite treatment, more than half of patients continue to suffer from symptoms 12 months after symptom onset, resulting in substantially reduced quality of life and work capacity (5). A major concern among patients is permanent vision loss due to optic nerve atrophy caused by sustained intracranial pressure. Although current therapeutic strategies effectively reduce the risk of vision loss, fear of this complication remains high. Patients are encouraged to monitor visual function closely to ensure timely intervention if deterioration occurs. However, this vigilance may inadvertently reinforce a cycle of heightened fear, inactivity, diminished quality of life, and increased risk of chronicity. In Denmark, a national reference program for the diagnosis and treatment of Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (IIH) has been established; however, it provides no non-pharmacological recommendations (6). While weight loss, exercise, and lifestyle modification are emphasized, clinical experience shows that many patients remain inactive due to fear of symptom exacerbation through movement. In a clinical setting, patients frequently report concern about head motion triggering headaches and neck pain for which they often seek medical advice, which imposes a considerable burden on both patients and healthcare services. At present, the program primarily focuses on diagnostic procedures and pharmacological treatment, leaving lifestyle recommendations unsupported by structured interventions. This may represent a substantial untapped potential in IIH management. Documenting differences in how this population moves their head, pain sensitivity and psychosocial factors such as fear of physical activity, compared with healthy controls, may support an update to the clinical recommendations to include non-pharmacological treatment strategies centered on physical activity, benefiting both the patients and healthcare system. The aim of the present study is twofold. First, to assess whether head movements (range of motion, movement speed and quality of motion) and pressure pain thresholds, both locally and distally, are different compared to the control group. Secondly, to explore the extent to which fear avoidance beliefs and kinesiophobia are associated with pain pressure thresholds and head movements. Method Data is expected to be collected between November 2025 to December 2026: 28 patients with IIH who are well-treated pharmacologically, but still have symptoms such as headache and neck pain , and 28matched healthy subjects by age, sex and and, as closely as possible, body mass index (BMI) and will be recruited for a 30-minute evaluation at the Pain and Headache Clinic at the University Hospital of Aarhus as a part of a quality assurance project. The evaluation consists of a questionnaire survey distributed via REDCap, including the following instruments: • Neck Disability Index (NDI) (7) • The Hospitality Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) (8) • Fear-avoidance beliefs questionnaire, physical activity subscale (FABQpa) (9) • Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia-13 (TSK-13) (10) • Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6) (11) The physical evaluation consists of an examination of head movements into rotation, flexion and extension, measured by a digital goniometer (12) and recording of pressure pain thresholds bilaterally at the upper trapezius muscle and at the extensor carpi radialis muscle at the right forearm, measured with a handheld pressure algometer (13). title: Performance and limitation of machine learning algorithms for diabetic retinopathy screening and its application in health management: a meta-analysis
description: Diabetes mellitus affects 463 million adults and consumes 1.8% of gross domestic product globally, posing a huge burden on healthcare systems, especially in remote, underserved areas. Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a vision-threatening condition that affects 22.27% of adults with diabetes. With the diabetes pandemic spreading from wealthy industrialized countries to developing regions, the number of people with DR will increase from 103.12 million in 2020 to 160.50 million in 2045. Visual impairment and blindness due to DR can be significantly reduced if diagnosed at an early stage and treated appropriately. However, due to the high cost and low accessibility of eye services, <70% of people with diabetes receive eye examinations at regular intervals. The current strategy for detecting DR is based on clinical examination by an ophthalmologist or grading of retinal photographs via telemedicine, which relies on highly trained staff or requires expensive equipment. In addition, whether the recommended screening interval can be extended has attracted extensive debate because a large number of DR-negative patients receive repeated annual fundus screenings. It was estimated that the DR service would be reduced by 40% if people with no visible retinopathy at two consecutive screens received 2-year rather than annual screening in the Scottish Diabetic Retinopathy Screening programme. The National Health Service Foundation Trust claimed that screening people with type 2 diabetes every 2 years, rather than annually, would reduce screening costs by 25%. Therefore, establishing simple, practical methods for identifying people at high risk of referable DR (RDR) based on easily accessible indicators has become an important goal, which will help to target screening and prevention. Modeling for RDR is challenging because most medical data has a non-linear, non-normal, and non-independent distribution, and traditional regression analysis techniques would lose information. The use of machine learning (ML) techniques offers an alternative solution, which captures the non-linear relationship in data without prior assumption. Furthermore, ML is able to rank variables by importance. Previous studies have demonstrated that ML-based methods can accurately identify diabetes in the general population. However, limited studies based on ML for DR classification are available to date.

title: Eye images do not promote prosocial behaviour or norm compliance in an online Dictator Game
description: Evidence for the effect of eye images on prosocial behavior is mixed: some studies have found that images of eyes enhance cooperative behavior while others have not replicated this effect. In a recent meta-analysis, Nettle et al. (2013) argued that previous null results have occurred because data have been analysed incorrectly. Specifically, the authors predicted that eye images either (i) reduce variance in donation amount by reducing the likelihood that the Dictator will keep the entire endowment or (ii) increase compliance with cooperative norms. Since several previous studies have only looked at the effect of eye images on mean donation amount, they have not tested these predictions. We test both hypotheses here using a Dictator Game (n = 779) conducted over Amazon Mechanical Turk, a setup that has previously yielded negative results. We provided players with two types of descriptive norm information, by telling them how much others typically give in this setting. We compared donations under the norm treatments with decisions made under control conditions, where no norm information was supplied. In each setting, subjects were additionally shown images of eyes or a control image (flowers) so that any additional effect of eye images on prosocial behavior could be examined. Eye images did not increase Dictator Game giving, regardless of whether 'giving' was defined as mean donation or simply the tendency to make a non-zero donation. Furthermore, eye images did not increase compliance with a descriptive norm in this setting. Due to these negative results, we conclude that the conditions and underlying mechanisms that lead to positive effects of eyes on prosocial behaviour remain elusive.

title: Social Structure Learning in Anterior Insula
description: Humans form social coalitions in every society, yet we know little about how we learn and represent social group boundaries. Here we derive predictions from a computational model of latent structure learning to move beyond explicit category labels and interpersonal, or dyadic similarity as the sole inputs to social group representations. Using a model-based analysis of functional neuroimaging data, we find that separate areas correlate with dyadic similarity and latent structure learning. Trial-by-trial estimates of 'allyship' based on dyadic similarity between participants and each agent recruited medial prefrontal cortex/pregenual anterior cingulate (pgACC). Latent social group structure-based allyship estimates, in contrast, recruited right anterior insula (rAI). Variability in the brain signal from rAI improved prediction of variability in ally-choice behavior, whereas variability from the pgACC did not. These results provide novel insights into the psychological and neural mechanisms by which people learn to distinguish "us" from "them."

title: A head-to-head comparison of narcissism measures' ability to predict emotion dysregulation
description: Narcissism can be defined as the "ability to regulate self-esteem and manage needs for affirmation, validation, and self-enhancement from the social environment" (Pincus & Lukowitsky, 2010). When this ability is impaired, individuals rely on rigid and maladaptive strategies to cope with perceived threats to self-esteem, a condition often referred as pathological narcissism (PN) (Pincus & Lukowitsky, 2010). Contemporary models define at least two sub-dimensions of PN, namely, grandiosity (characterized by self-enhancement strategies such as self-overvaluation, entitlement, exploitative and exhibitionistic behaviors, absorption in idealized fantasies) and vulnerability (characterized by a depleted self-image, angry, depressed and shameful affects, hypersensitivity to criticism, emotional instability, and social withdrawal) (Pincus & Lukowitsky, 2010). The diagnostic category traditionally associated with PN is narcissistic personality disorder (NPD), which primarily captures overt grandiose features (Cain et al., 2008). Furthermore, recent hierarchical models also propose a trifactorial structure underlying both grandiose and vulnerable narcissism, with three components: antagonism, agentic extraversion, and narcissistic neuroticism (Crowe et al., 2019; Miller et al., 2021). First, antagonism is shared by both grandiosity and vulnerability, and includes entitlement, arrogance, exploitation, callousness, deceitfulness, and a fundamentally adversarial orientation toward others. Second, agentic extraversion is more specific to grandiosity and encompasses dominance, assertiveness, social boldness, high self-confidence, and a strong orientation toward status and admiration. Finally, narcissistic neuroticism, more central to vulnerable narcissism, reflects emotional instability, shame, and hypersensitivity to self-esteem threats (Miller et al., 2021). Emotion dysregulation (ED) refers to a multidimensional pattern of difficulties in how individuals understand, accept, and modulate their emotional responses (Blay, Duarte, et al., 2024; McRae &Gross, 2020). Six main components of emotion regulation difficulties have been described by Gratz and Roemer and are operationalized in the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS), the most commonly used scale to assess ED in clinical research (Gratz & Roemer, 2004). This model emphasizes that ED is not limited to emotional intensity but rather reflects impairments across multiple stages of emotional processing and regulation: lack of emotional awareness (i.e., difficulties to pay attention to and acknowledge one's emotions), lack of emotional clarity (i.e., difficulties in making sense out of and in labeling, identifying, or differentiating emotional experiences), non-acceptance of emotional responses (i.e., tendencies to judge emotional experiences), difficulties engaging in goal-directed behavior under emotions (i.e., problems with keeping concentration and focus, and pursuing work or purposeful goals), impulse control difficulties (i.e., reduced ability to inhibit inappropriate or harmful behaviors, feeling overwhelmed and out of control under emotional states,), and limited access to emotion regulation strategies (i.e., believing that nothing can alleviate emotional distress and lack of perceived or actual strategies to modulate emotions once they are activated). In a recent systematic review, we found that individuals presenting with higher narcissistic vulnerability tend to show greater difficulties in regulating emotions, whereas those presenting with higher grandiose narcissism show more inconsistent associations, the discordant results being often linked to the tools used to assess narcissism (Blay, Cham, et al., 2024). Regarding ED facets, results were highly inconsistent between studies for both dimensions, partly for the same psychometric reasons. For example, we found that vulnerable narcissism often showed positive associations with clarity, non-acceptance, impulse control, and strategies subdomains (when assessed with both Hypersensitive Narcissism Scale – HSNS - and the Pathological Narcissism Inventory - PNI), but also with awareness and goals (only when assessed with the PNI). Unfortunately, this high heterogeneity prevailed any conclusion regarding the association between specific facets of ED and narcissism. Moreover, these psychometric limitations were not the only one we found in the current literature on the link between PN and ED. Most studies used one-factor (narcissism) or two-factors (grandiosity vs vulnerability) tools to assess narcissism, whereas none used NPD or three-factor (agentic extraversion, antagonism, narcissistic neuroticism) measures. Finally, only two studies adjusted their analysis on comorbid borderline personality disorder (BPD) or symptomatology, a disorder that is strongly associated with narcissistic vulnerability (Euler et al., 2018) and emotional dysregulation (Glenn & Klonsky, 2009), and some who did so found a confounding effect of this comorbidity on the observed associations (Blay, Bouteloup, et al., 2024). Together, these limitations impede clarity and complicate the interpretation of findings regarding the links between PN and ED. To start addressing this issue, there is a critical need to directly compare multiple narcissism measures, including NPD and three-factor measures, on their relationship to ED, specifically the comparative predictive values of these measures. The present study aims to conduct such a head-to-head comparison, using four common narcissism measures: the DSM-5 NPD criteria (American Psychiatric Association, 2013), the PNI in its brief form (Diguer et al., 2020; Schoenleber et al., 2015), the Maladaptive Covert Narcissism Scale (MCNS) (Cheek et al., 2013), and the Five-Factor Narcissism Inventory (FFNI) in its super-short form (Packer West et al., 2021). These measures all capture different aspects of narcissism. NPD criteria are well-known to capture mostly overt grandiosity, with a sole focus on paradigmatic externalized manifestations that neglect vulnerability (Blay et al., 2025; Cain et al., 2008; Miller et al., 2021). On the other hand, the PNI assess both grandiosity and vulnerability, but its grandiosity subscale is considered to not grasp "pure" narcissistic grandiosity given its considerable overlap with the vulnerability subscale (Edershile et al., 2019). Furthermore, the MCNS specifically assesses covert narcissistic vulnerability, and focuses mainly on internal processes such as shame, rumination, or rage (Cheek et al., 2013; Miller et al., 2021). Finally, the FFNI is aligned with contemporary structural models of narcissism and assesses grandiosity and vulnerability, as well as antagonism, agentic extraversion, and narcissistic neuroticism (Miller et al., 2021). Using such a variety of instruments, including categorical, two-factor and three-factor conceptualizations of narcissism, allows for a more nuanced and integrative exploration of how different facets of PN may relate to ED and its components. Altogether, our primary objective is to clarify the heterogeneous associations between pathological narcissism and emotion dysregulation by directly comparing categorical, two-factor, and three-factor narcissism models in their associations with overall and domain specific emotion dysregulation in a clinical population. As a secondary aim, we will assess whether these associations remain after accounting for borderline personality disorder symptoms, given its estalished links with both narcissistic vulnerability and emotion dysregulation.

title: The Magnitude and Time-Course of Foveal Bias in Ensemble Perception
description: Humans can quickly estimate the statistical properties of visual features in the environment. Recent studies have shown that not all elements in a visual ensemble contribute equally to the estimated summary statistic. Rather, ensemble perception is biased towards items near the fovea. In the present experiment, we plan to investigate whether the magnitude of foveal bias observed in ensemble perception is influenced by on-going eye movements and the time-course of stimulus presentation after foveation. Participants will be asked to view an ensemble of oriented lines and report their average orientation after making a saccade or fixating at a cued location. After fixation or saccade landing, the ensemble could be presented immediately or after a delay of 50 ms, 100 ms, or 200 ms. Ensemble items at the center of gaze could correspond to one of three standard ensemble quadrants, with orientations drawn from the same uniform distribution, or to an outlier quadrant, with orientations drawn from a uniform distribution whose mean is shifted by 37.5° relative to the standard quadrants. We will examine whether participant responses are biased towards foveated items and analyse whether this bias is impacted by saccadic eye movements as well as temporal delays between foveation and ensemble presentation.

title: Evaluation of Linguistic Variability of Large Language Model Text Personalization Using Natural Language Processing
description: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is proposed in this paper as an evaluation framework to track linguistic patterns of Large Language Models (LLMs) outputs over time. NLP metrics were used to quantify and compare the differences in repeated generation using the same prompt. Experiment 1 examined internal reliability across 10 repeated generations of four LLMs (i.e., Claude, Llama, Gemini, ChatGPT) on 10 scientific texts tailored for a reader profile. Linear mixed-effects models showed no effect of repeated trial on linguistic features (e.g., cohesion, syntactic complexity, lexical diversity, lexical sophistication, noun-to-verb ratios, sentence length, writing style). The results indicated high short-term stability but robust linguistic patterns between LLMs, suggesting unique writing style. Experiment 2 assessed linguistic variation using standardized prompts on GPT-4o (deployed in Oct 2024 versus Jun 2025) and GPT-4.1 (deployed in Jun 2025), with adaptations tailored for four hypothetical reader profiles. Significant differences in linguistic behavior was detected across model updates over time. GPT-4o (Jun 2025) produced shorter, more cohesive outputs with reduced language variety (greater consistency), whereas GPT-4.1 (Jun 2025) produced more academic, lexically sophisticated text with higher noun-to-verb ratios and longer sentences (more formal writing style). LLMs are updated quickly and frequently, yet there is currently no standardized method for tracking their linguistic patterns. The current study demonstrated the capability of NLP-based evaluation methods for detecting meaningful linguistic changes across LLM updates.

In the United States and Europe, the prevalence has doubled over the last half-century with half of young adults now having myopia[1]. The consequence of myopia extends beyond the inconvenience of using optical correction. Myopia is associated with increased incidence of diseases such as retinal damage, cataract, and glaucoma [1]. Increased levels of near-work have commonly been associated with the onset of myopia [2]. It is therefore important to gain a better understanding of what is happening from a functional and anatomical standpoint when subjects complete near-work tasks. There are two different types of text, texts that have positive contrast (white text on a darker background) and texts that have negative contrast (black text on a lighter background). Aleman et. al (2018) found that negative contrast texts produced a thinning effect on the choroid (-16.13土4.54 μm), and positive contrast produced a thickening effect on the choroid(9.96土 6.51μm) [3]. Aleman et. al interpreted these results in the context of ON and OFF pathways in the visual system [4]. They suggested negative contrast texts stimulate the OFF pathway, while positive contrast texts stimulate the ON pathway. Choroidal thickening and thinning in both chicks and marmosets has been observed to be a precursor to a decrease or an increase in axial growth respectively [5, 6, 7]. The latter leading to the development of myopia. Trolio et. al documented 20 μm of choroidal thinning in myopia induced marmoset eyes and 12 μm of thickening in eyes induced with hyperopia [5]. It is hypothesized that the choroid either acts as a mechanical buffer or a diffusion barrier for the sclera [5]. Qualitatively, Aleman et al's data showed the thinning effect was more pronounced in myopic individuals as compared to their emmetropic counterparts [3], but their sample size was insufficient to draw quantitative conclusions. The plasticity of the human choroid is an important link to animal models. For example, Read et. al found that among a group of 39 myopic individuals subfoveal choroidal thickness was 50 μm thinner than nonmyopic age-matched children [8]. Retinal Ganglion Cells are organized in an ON center OFF surround arrangement or vice versa [2]. ON cells become depolarized to an increment in light, while OFF depolarize in response to decrements in light. OFF retinal ganglion cells are twice as numerous and half the size of ON rental ganglion cells in the fovea. Several studies such as Mazade et. al, Lu et. al, and Tyler et. al corroborated the different spatial tuning and cortical connectivity of the ON and OFF pathway [9, 10, 11]. Mazade et al showed maximal cortical responses for small fast stimuli in the OFF pathway and maximal cortical responses for slow slow global stimuli in the ON pathway [10]. Zhong-Lin et. al found negative stimuli (or decrements in light) to be 25% more effective than equal magnitude positive stimuli (or increments in light) across eleven different types of stimuli [11]. Taken together, these studies support a distinct roles for the ON and OFF pathways in the visual system. The goal of our study is threefold. We aim to replicate the changes in choroidal thickness in response to negative and positive contrast with a larger subject group. We aim to measure the sensitivity to positive and negative contrast tasks and compare the ratio of contrast sensitivity to these two contrast types among refractive error/axial length. Finally, we will monitor the changes in sensitivity to positive and negative contrast as the session proceeds as to understand the functional implications choroidal thickness changes may have.

title: Use of deep learning-based optic chiasm segmentation for the investigation of visual system pathophysiology and neuroplasticity
description: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models are of great promise to aid segmentation and analysis of brain structures. Here, we tested, whether CNN trained to segment normal optic chiasms from T1w MRI image can be also applied to abnormal chiasms, specifically with optic nerve misrouting as typical for human albinism. We performed supervised training of the CNN on the T1w images of control participants (n=1049) from Human Connectome Project repository and automatically generated algorithm-based optic chiasm masks. The trained CNN was subsequently tested on data of persons with albinism (PWA; n=9) and controls (n=8) from the CHIASM repository. The quality of outcome segmentation was assessed via the comparison to manually defined optic chiasm masks using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC). The results revealed contrasting quality of masks obtained for control (mean DSC ± SEM = 0.75 ± 0.03) and PWA data (0.43 ± 0.8, FWE corrected p=0.04). The fact that the CNN recognition of the optic chiasm fails for chiasm abnormalities in PWA underlines the fundamental differences in their spatial features. This finding thus provides proof-of-concept for a novel deep-learning based diagnostics-approach of chiasmal misrouting from T1w images, as well as further analyses on chiasmal misrouting and their impact on structure and function of visual system.

title: Teacher Expectations of Literacy Instruction for Students with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities
description: Note: Project originally pre-registered Oct 12, 2022. Withdrew and re-registered, on April 7, 2023, according to OSF protocol, due to error in original Contributor list (i.e., PI not included). See internet archive Iink: https://archive.org/details/osf-registrations-x5gjc-v1 Historically, students with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) have had limited access to rigorous reading instruction. Past emphases have included whole-word reading, isolated skill practice, and functional reading skills (Browder et al., 2006). However, updated research provides evidence that students with IDD can benefit from rigorous reading instruction that is inclusive of a wider set of objectives (Browder et al., 2009). Translation of such research into practice may be influenced by teachers' knowledge and perceptions of reading instruction for students with IDD, who may receive special education services under the categories of intellectual disability, autism, developmental delay, or multiple disabilities. Previous research indicates that teachers vary in their knowledge of reading development and instruction, in some cases with special education teachers demonstrating greater knowledge of these concepts than general education colleagues (see Bos et al., 2001). More recent research (Porter et al., 2021), suggests that reading specialists may be more knowledgeable on this topic than general education teachers, who are in turn more knowledgeable than special education teachers. Such findings are concerning, given that all educators need to be aware of reading development and instructional methods to meet the needs of students who require a range of supports. In conjunction with knowledge of reading, teacher perceptions of student abilities have been demonstrated to predict classroom instruction and student reading success (e.g., Bos et al., 2001; Piasta et al., 2009; Ruppar et al., 2015). Students with IDD tend to receive instruction from special education teachers and often paraprofessionals. Educators with higher knowledge of reading development and higher expectations for their students are more likely to use evidence-based instructional methods that ensure greater student growth. Such instructional decisions are sometimes decided by school or intermediate unit (IU) administrators. Therefore, it is important to collect data not only on what teachers know about reading instruction, but also what they believe students with IDD are capable of learning. The purpose of this study is to develop and validate an initial measure of teacher expectations for reading instruction for students with intellectual and developmental disabilities. There is no tool to date that measures teachers' expectations for literacy instruction, taking into consideration the specific needs and characteristics of students with IDD. This measure will be called the Teacher Expectations in Literacy for Students with IDD (TELSIDD) scale. This initial measure will be validated using exploratory factor analysis methods. Following validation, we anticipate conducting future studies to further explore the validity and dimensionality of the measure, using confirmatory analyses.

title: Accuracy of Intraoperative Surgical Margin Assessment Techniques in Veterinary Oncology
description: Accurate determination of surgical margin status is fundamental for detecting residual microscopic residual cancer in patients, predicting clinical outcomes, and optimizing treatment planning. Postoperative histopathology following surgical tumor resection is considered the gold standard for margin evaluation; however, this process typically takes one or two weeks to obtain results and only a limited sample of the surgical margins are assessed. Consequently, this delay results in a missed opportunity to evaluate surgical margins in real time and to utilize that information for immediate intraoperative decision-making, which could improve patient outcomes. Several techniques are available for intraoperative surgical margin assessment, each with different levels of accuracy, including frozen tissue section biopsy, imprint cytology margin, near-infrared fluorescence imaging, and optical coherence tomography (OCT) which has the potential to guide surgical-decision making in real-time. This review aims to compare the diagnostic accuracy of intraoperative surgical margin evaluation techniques as individual studies focus on the reporting of accuracy of one technique in comparison to histopathology. Only studies on canine cutaneous or subcutaneous tumors will be included in the review. The primary outcome of the review is comparison of diagnostic accuracy for detection of positive surgical margins in cutaneous and subcutaneous tumors across techniques.

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence for Retinopathy of Prematurity: A Systematic Review
description: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) remains an important cause of childhood blindness. It occurs when premature birth results in avascular peripheral retina up-regulating the production of vascular growth factors in the extra-uterine environment, resulting in pathological fibrovascular proliferation. This process is exacerbated by additional factors such as low birth weight and the use of supplemental oxygen. Proper screening of neonates at risk is necessary to identify those who may need treatment. The current standard of care for detecting ROP is indirect ophthalmoscopy of the peripheral retina after pupillary dilation. In regions where access to ophthalmologists is limited, delayed detection of ROP progression and the resulting lack of timely intervention leads to permanent blindness. With the advent of telemedicine programs, fundus photography and computer based analysis of these images can be used to provide adequate care for those in need. Over the past decade, software programs involving the use of artificial intelligence have been developed with the goal of improving screening and diagnosis of ROP. The purpose of this literature review is to summarize the developments in this field and assess their efficacy in comparison to indirect ophthalmoscopy.

title: DEEP LEARNING FOR AUTOMATED DETECTION AND CLASSIFICATION OF TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINT DISORDERS: A SCOPING REVIEW
description: Title: Deep Learning for Automated Detection and Classification of Temporomandibular Joint Disorders: A Scoping Review Temporomandibular Joint Disorders (TMDs) are a significant clinical challenge associated with pain, functional impairment, and reduced quality of life. Traditional diagnostic approaches—such as manual interpretation of MRI, CBCT, CT, or panoramic images—can be time-consuming, subjective, and affected by inter-observer variability. With recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL) techniques, automated detection and classification of TMDs has emerged as a promising solution to enhance diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. This scoping review systematically maps current evidence on deep learning applications for diagnosing TMDs, including anterior disc displacement (ADD), osteoarthritis, condylar degeneration, and degenerative joint disease. Using PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a comprehensive search across PubMed, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and Wiley identified 15 eligible studies published between 2015 and 2025. Across these studies, models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), U-Net, ResNet, VGG16, MobileNetV2, YOLO, and ensemble architectures demonstrated high diagnostic performance—achieving accuracy levels up to 99%, sensitivity up to 98%, and significant improvements in segmentation precision. Findings indicate that deep learning can reduce diagnostic time by up to 50%, standardize interpretation, and serve as an effective decision-support tool for clinicians. Despite promising results, challenges remain related to dataset diversity, external validation, reproducibility, and clinical integration. Future research should focus on multi-center datasets, multimodal learning, standardized benchmarking, explainability methods such as Grad-CAM, and ethical frameworks for AI deployment in healthcare. This review highlights the potential of deep learning to transform TMD diagnostics, contributing to faster, more accurate, and more consistent radiologic evaluation, ultimately improving clinical outcomes for patients.

description: Relational Field Theory (RFT) predicts that coherence shared across physically separated signal paths can induce a measurable modification to apparent group delay, without signal energy transfer or classical synchronization. We present the first bench-ready validation protocol for the Coherence Web – Time Compression (CW-TC) phenomenon. Two channels, REF and TEST, are driven with identical source patterns, while a third signal, the Coherence Reference Apparatus (CRA), injects phase-stable relational coherence without exchanging carrier information. When TEST entrains to the CRA field, its effective propagation delay shifts by δτ , observable via stable cross-correlation peak movement. The effect disappears when CRA is disabled, reverses sign under a π phase flip, and scales monotonically with coherence amplitude. These results satisfy six independent falsifiers, distinguishing relational coherence from RF leakage, DSP bias, or shared-clock artifacts. The experiment provides reproducible, physics-level evidence that coherence itself can modify timing, supporting the Coherence Law derivations central to RFT 2.0. title: Systematic Review of the A2 Segment of Anterior Cerebral Artery
description: Anterior cerebral artery (ACA) is a terminal branch of the internal carotid artery, passes around corpus callosum up to the splenium and supplies frontal, pre-frontal and supplementary motor cortex. ACA is divided into five segments. This review focuses only on the A2 segment of ACA called post-communicating segment, which originates at the anterior communicating artery and extends anterior to the lamina terminalis. The termination of this segment is abigous in the literature and some authors described ending of the A2 segment (1) at the junction of the rostrum and genu of corpus callosum, or (2) at the bifurcation of ACA forming by origin of the callosomarginal and pericallosal artery. Current reviews mostly described one type of information about the anatomy of A2 segment. The aim of this systematic review is to comprehensively synthesize the available evidence concerning (1) the prevalence and differences branching patterns and anatomical variations of the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) A2 segment, its (2) topography relationships with adjacent neurovascular structures, and (3) the cortical and subcortical territories supplied by its branches. This systematic review provides an evidence-based synthesis to guide anatomical understanding and clinical practice which is essential for safe surgical approaches to anterior communicating artery complex and medial frontal lobe.

title: Justice is in the Eyes of the Beholder IV: Coherence Shifts (lab)
description: Judges are obliged to justify the decisions they make. Judges are supposed to be impartial. One purpose of written justifications is to check for impartiality. This would be straightforward if written reasons were a faithful representation of the mental process that led the judge to her decision. A precondition for an argument brought forward by one of the parties to affect the judge's decision is the judge paying attention to the argument. Arguably the more the judge pays attention, the greater the impact of the argument. The number and the duration of fixations on items is a good proxy for attention. If there were a close mapping between mental process and the reasons expressed in the ruling, the more the judge fixates on the item representing an argument, the more importance she should give this argument in the reasons of her ruling. In an earlier study we have found that, actually, eye gaze and stated relevance are uncorrelated. The same also holds for stated difficulty in understanding the argument, stated degree of ambiguity, and stated degree of conflict with other arguments. However, eye gaze strongly predicts decisions. We take this as evidence that the mental process of discovery, and the representation of the result, are autonomous activities. As an ex post rationalisation, we propose that the decision is found by way of parallel constraint satisfaction. Decision makers are not aware of this subconscious process. A new study serves two purposes: 1. We want to put this ex post rationalisation to the test. 2. We want to gain insight into the mental process that leads to the formation of the decision. We are, in particular, interested in the importance of attention on arguments that speak against the ultimate ruling. This study tests whether we do indeed find parallel constraint satisfaction. If true, we should see that participants reweight the arguments after they have made their decision, and reweighting should be mirrored in eye gaze.

title: Human Breastmilk in Ocular Health and Disease: A Scoping Review Protocol
description: This scoping review seeks to provide a comprehensive mapping of the existing body of knowledge on the application of human breastmilk within the domain of ocular health and disease. The review will examine the documented antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, wound-healing and broader therapeutic properties of breastmilk as they relate to a range of ocular conditions, including neonatal conjunctivitis, ocular surface disorders, corneal ulceration and other external eye infections. In addition, attention will be given to the perceived risks, underlying cultural practices, modes of administration and the extent to which current evidence substantiates the clinical use of breastmilk in eye care. Guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) framework for scoping reviews, this study will systematically identify, chart and synthesise available literature to elucidate the mechanisms of action, reported clinical outcomes, safety considerations and existing gaps in the evidence base. The review is expected to generate an informative overview that will support clinicians, researchers and public health practitioners in understanding the current landscape of evidence and in identifying priority areas for future inquiry.

title: The Topography of Daily Impulsivity
description: Impulsivity, or the tendency to behave with little to no forethought or consideration of the consequences, holds significant public health relevance (Whiteside & Lynam, 2001). It is associated with a host of psychological and physical health conditions, such as borderline personality disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, eating disorders, addiction, and obesity, and is the most frequently included feature of psychopathology across diagnoses listed in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (American Psychiatric Association [APA], 2013; Mullins-Sweatt et al., 2019; Schweren et al., 2021). Although impulsivity has traditionally been studied using cross-sectional self-report measures, it is a dynamic phenomenon and global self-report designs do not allow for a study of the contexts and contingencies that influence its manifestation. Over the recent decades, research has turned to ecological momentary assessment (EMA) techniques to study impulsivity dynamically and in context (e.g., Feil et al., 2020; Sharpe et al., 2021; Sperry et al., 2018, 2021). At the same time, a different line of work has explored the momentary distribution of psychological phenomena, such as emotion, and their link to other relevant behaviors and constructs (e.g., Heller et al., 2021; Thompson et al., 2012; Trull et al., 2015). Despite the centrality of impulsive tendencies not only for psychopathology but also for daily behaviors, very few studies have examined the link between the distribution of daily impulsivity and trait levels of impulsivity. In an EMA study in a sample of people with borderline personality disorder (BPD) or depressive disorder (DD), Tomko and colleagues (2014) calculated the average of daily mean squared successive difference (MSSD) to capture temporal dependency and variability of state impulsivity. Their findings suggested that participants endorsing higher levels of trait impulsivity also had higher MSSD scores compared to those with lower levels of trait impulsivity. The results also showed that for people with BPD, correlations between average daily impulsivity scores and trait impulsivity scores were stronger than those between trait impulsivity and MSSD; the reverse was true for the DD group. While this study highlighted the complex nature of between- versus within-group associations, research on impulsivity variability has been quite limited. To our knowledge, no study to date has examined the association between the distribution of daily impulsivity and daily behaviors and contextual information. Exploring indices of variability in state impulsivity can provide valuable insights into the dynamics of impulsivity and how it may interact with contextual factors in real life to shape behavior. To address this gap, we aim to explore the association between self-reports of trait impulsivity and indices of variability (dispersion from the central tendency) in state impulsivity. We also plan to examine the association between state impulsivity and other daily behaviors and contextual factors, including day of the week, time of day, location, activity, number of social interactions and interaction partner, and sleep duration. Additionally, given the known role of demographic factors in the manifestation of impulsivity (Cross et al., 2011; Paál et al., 2015; Steinberg et al., 2008), we aim to investigate the association between daily impulsivity and specific demographic factors, including age, sex, education level, employment status, income level, and relationship status.
