title: Leading Towards a Translation Readiness Framework: A Systematic Review of Deep Learning Approaches for Eye Diseases Diagnosis
description: Background: Artificial intelligence has significantly improved the diagnosis of retinal diseases using fundus and optical coherence tomography. However, the pathway between the accuracy of the models and their clinical application is still unclear. Objectives: The main objective of this systematic review is to overcome this gap by correlating the quality of methodology with clinical preparation in the current studies and to critically examine the translation readiness possibility. Methods: The PRISMA-based review clearly addresses the six research questions in an organized manner. A comprehensive search is conducted across six electronic databases, resulting in a total of 883 records. After rigorous screening, a final set of 43 fundus- and OCT-based articles published between 2020 and August 2025 and passing a comprehensive eligibility criterion are selected. The selected studies are assessed using the custom AI-specific risk-of-bias assessment tool and the CLAIM checklist to measure the quality of technical reporting. The reviewer's agreement is calculated using Cohen's kappa, interrater reliability, and the intraclass correlation coefficient. Results: Although convolutional and hybrid deep-learning-based studies are often reported to have an accuracy of more than 95.0%, only 14.3% are truly clinically validated, and 23.1% do not include code or implementation data details. Reviewers' agreement scores are from moderate to high (fundus-based ICC(2,1)=0.911, ICC(2,1)=0.911,CI=[0.896,0.923]) and (OCT based ICC(2,1)=0.643, CI=[0.422,0.792]), supporting the reliability of the quality assessments. In order to combine these dimensions, we come up with a composite Technical-Clinical Integrity Index, which measures data transparency, rigor of validation, and reporting of performance. Conclusion: Retinal disease diagnosis has achieved high performance with low clinical transfer. This review provides the guidelines of a Translational Readiness Framework that can be used by researchers, clinicians, and health-analytics teams to assess and implement credible artificial intelligence systems in ophthalmology.

title: Eye movements and recognition memory
description: Eye movements, such as saccades and fixations, shape memory processes and affect the neural activity in hippocampal and adjacent medial temporal lobe regions associated with memory (Bicanski & Burgess, 2019). In turn, eye movements rely on the integrity of medial temporal lobe areas, reflecting a bidirectional link between the oculomotor and the memory system (Lucas et al., 2019; Meister & Buffalo, 2016). Hippocampal activation and memory performance positively scale with the number of eye movements that participants perform when visually exploring a presented image (Fehlmann et al., 2020). What is unclear is whether this is tied to specific patterns of eye movements, such as revisitations (i.e., the number of times participants revisit and thus re-encode image parts that were previously viewed; Kragel et al., 2021). Moreover, how revisitation patterns are associated with hippocampal activity is not fully understood. Here, we aim to investigate the relation between revisitation patterns, recognition memory, and activation changes in brain regions associated with visuo-oculomotor- (i.e., the visual cortex, V1, and the frontal eye fields, FEF) and memory-related processes (i.e., hippocampal, HC, and medial temporal lobe regions such as the entorhinal cortex, EC). To determine whether brain regions involved in stimulus-specific processing, including the parahippocampal place (PPA) and the fusiform face area (FFA) are similarly affected, we examine eye-movement-related brain activation in these areas as well. The data for this study have already been collected. Fifty healthy participants (aged 18-35 years) studied face and scene images while undergoing functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and continuous eye tracking (ET). To assess memory performance, participants completed a recognition memory task immediately after study and one week after.

title: Why worse detection performance in with-contour condition? : A further examination
description: In a previous experiment (see pre-registration osf.io/weag6), we found that although the accuracy of memorizing four distinct discs with subjective contours (with-contour condition) was better than that of memorizing four distinct discs without subjective contours (without-contour condition), the dectection to the peripheral target was worse in with-contour condition than that in the without-contour condition. First, all the discs orientated centrally in the with-contour condition, directing participants' attention to a narrow space; whereas the discs in the without-countour condition were oriented to the peripheral space. This stimuli setting may contaminate our finding. Second, the central exceutive load is higher in the without-contour condition than that in the with-contour condition, leading to higher detection performance according to the load theory (Lavie, 2005). The current study aims to test the two alternatives from a new perspective. We required participants to retain four distinct discs with subjective countours (with-countour condition), four distinct discs without subjective countours (without-countour condition), or two distinct discs without subjective countours (load-two condition). Critically, with-countour condition and without-countour condition shared the same set of stimuli, and all oriented centrally.

description: Abstract Background: Diabetic retinopathy is not only the most common complication of diabetes, but also one of the main causes of blindness, which seriously affects the physical and mental health of patients. Discussion: This study will evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of Qiming granule combined with laser in the treatment of diabetic retinopathy. title: Minimum Semantic Content (MSC) image dataset, a balanced dataset containing "ugly" images (alongside more traditionally appealing ones) of objects with little semantic content
description: The Minimum Semantic Content (MSC) dataset provides a structured resource aimed at isolating aesthetic judgments from cognitive (semantic) influences, making it particularly useful for advancing empirical studies on aesthetics. Unlike existing image datasets that predominantly feature beautiful images, the MSC dataset offers a balanced selection of 10,426 images, carefully curated span the whole range from "ugly" to "beautiful". The images were also selected to minimize semantic content. This reduction allows researchers to focus on perceptual factors underlying aesthetic judgments, avoiding the confounding influence of complex cognitive associations. Each image in the MSC dataset has been evaluated by 100 observers, ensuring robust data on aesthetic ratings. By including comparable amounts of "beautiful" and "ugly" images, the MSC dataset enables a re-examination of relationships between low-level image features and aesthetic valuations. This expanded aesthetic range offers insights that challenge or refine current models, demonstrating that limiting datasets to predominantly beautiful images can skew, exaggerate, or miss significant findings on the aesthetic response to image content. Each of the 10,426 images in the MSC dataset has been evaluated by 100 observers, ensuring robust data on aesthetic ratings. By including a method for generating "ugly" images alongside more traditionally appealing ones, the MSC dataset enables a re-examination of relationships between low-level image features and aesthetic valuations. We provide a .csv file with raw crowdsourcing results, with each column representing the number of votes received for each of the five aesthetic valuation categories (1 = very ugly, 5 = very beautiful). we also provide results from truncated histogram fittings to the crowdsourcing data. These columns include the final value of mu (mean), the final value of sigma (standard deviation), the final FVAL and ExitFlag values from Matlab's fminsearch function, and the number of iterations required. Images were modified by observers. We provide categorization columns, specifying whether an image is "uglified," "beautified," "auto_uglified," or "unmodified." This section also indicates if an image served as the starting point for a modification (e.g., "uglified_original" denotes an image used as the basis for an uglification process). This structure ensures that users can easily identify the type and provenance of each image, as well as access comprehensive metadata and aesthetic ratings for further analysis.

title: Protocol for a scoping review on transient osteoporosis, bone marrow edema syndrome and related conditions
description: Proper classification plays an important role in defining the diagnosis, mechanisms and treatment of diseases. Logical discussion requires that patients with the same disease receive the same label. This issue is relevant for closely related disease concepts called transient osteoporosis of the hip (TOH), regional migratory osteoporosis (RMO), bone marrow edema syndrome (BMES) or localized osteoporosis (LO). Many other terms have also been used, see below. Patients who receive any of these diagnoses appear to have spontaneous joint pain, commonly in the lower limbs such as the hip or knee, and varying degree of local bone demineralization and/or bone marrow edema on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Spontaneous recovery seems to be common. Very little is known about epidemiology, etiology or pathophysiology. It has been questioned whether all the designations and labels really represent discrete disease entities, or are manifestations of a common, underlying pathology [1-6]. These conditions are rare, and the literature consists of scattered reports of single cases and small case series published over the last 60 years. The existing literature has, however, not been systematically reviewed or synthesized. Spurious labelling and inconsistent terminology hinder effective research and communication. Currently this field is confusing for clinicians, researchers, patients and the public. The aims of this scoping review are to (i) assess whether the designated terms (TOH, RMO, BMES and LO) clinically meaningful, and (ii) suggest changes if necessary.

title: Factors Driving Investment Regret
description: Standard approaches measure regret as a monotonic function of the difference between the realized return and the return of a foregone better alternative (reference point). We analyze additional factors that might have an influence on experienced regret in an investment context. To this end, we set up an observational study. Through an online survey, participants build a portfolio consisting of two stocks and are compensated based on the portfolio return. Given their return and that of foregone alternatives, we ask for their feeling of regret. In detail, we address four specific topics: • Is the plausibility of choice alternatives related to their acceptance as reference points and does it influence the experience of regret? • Is there a difference in experienced regret and rejoice if investors can justify their portfolio decision using standard theoretical reasoning compared to a decision based on subjective beliefs? • Does the level of research effort prior to the portfolio choice influence experienced regret and rejoice? • Do investors with stronger preferences for sustainable investments experience less regret than those with weaker preferences for sustainable investments?

title: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP): diagnostic accuracy of AI on retinal imaging for plus disease using wide-field retinal fundus photos
description: This study is a systematic review and meta-analysis examining the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)–based models for detecting plus disease and treatment-requiring retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) in preterm infants. ROP remains one of the leading causes of preventable childhood blindness, and identification of plus disease is central to treatment decisions. However, assessment based on wide-field digital retinal imaging (WFDRI) is subject to inter-observer variability and depends heavily on the availability of experienced ophthalmic graders. AI-driven image analysis has been proposed as a scalable approach to support screening and improve diagnostic consistency. The review will be conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidance. A comprehensive search will be performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science up to November 2025, with additional screening of reference lists. Eligible studies include original peer-reviewed human investigations evaluating AI algorithms applied to wide-field retinal fundus images, using expert human grading as the reference standard. Outcomes of interest include diagnostic accuracy measures such as sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Study selection, data extraction, and methodological quality assessment will be undertaken independently by multiple reviewers using standardized appraisal tools, including the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for diagnostic test accuracy studies.

title: The influence of physical exercise as an adjuvant strategy in the management of primary open-angle glaucoma (EYE-FIT project)
description: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible vision loss worldwide, which is caused by a progressive damage of the optic nerve. The control of intraocular pressure (IOP) levels is the only proven strategy for glaucoma management. In particular, the role of physical activity in IOP levels is mediated by the type of training performed. However, no previous study has assessed the impact of a structured physical training program on glaucoma progression. The general objective of this project is to provide effective training strategies to increase physical fitness without compromising or even improving the ocular health of pharmacologically treated primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) patients. 70 POAG patients will participate in a randomized controlled clinical trial consisting of 54 sessions performed during a 28-week period (4 pre-intervention assessment, 4 post-intervention assessment and 48 training sessions). Pre and post-training intervention assessments will include visual signs and visual-related symptomatology, as well as functional status (strength and endurance fitness). Training sessions will last 1 hour, including strength and endurance exercises (concurrent training).

title: Fatores relacionados à eficácia terapêutica no tratamento fonoaudiológico das disfonias: uma revisão de escopo
description: Essa revisão sistemática deverá se apoiar na seguinte pergunta norteadora: "Quais os fatores relacionados à efetividade terapêutica no tratamento fonoaudiológico para os diversos tipos de disfonias?". As orientações metodológicas a serem seguidas serão baseadas no manual de revisões sistemáticas do Joanna Briggs Institute (AROMATARIS e MUNN, 2020) e no PRISMA (GALVÃO et al, 2015) e cumprirá as etapas de Busca dos artigos, Seleção dos artigos e Análise dos resultados. A busca dos artigos será realizada de forma eletrônica e manual. Para a busca eletrônica as fontes de evidência serão as bases de dados Embase, Lilacs, Medline, Scopus e Web of Science. A busca manual será realizada nas referências dos artigos selecionados. A estratégia de busca a ser utilizada nas bases de dados deverá ser construída a partir do acrônimo PICO: Population/População, Intervention/Intervenção, Comparison/Comparação e Outcomes/Desfechos. Os termos serão definidos de acordo com os critérios de elegibilidade para os estudos, definidos pela equipe de pesquisa e catalogados nas bases de dados Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) e Embase subject headings (Emtree). As etapas de busca, seleção e extração dos dados de interesse serão realizadas por dois autores independentes. As discordâncias deverão ser resolvidas por um terceiro avaliador. A seleção será efetuada em duas etapas, primeiro examinando títulos e resumos a fim de aplicar os critérios de seleção, e depois com a leitura do texto completo para aplicação dos critérios de exclusão. Para reforçar a confiabilidade dos resultados, os artigos serão revisados por todos os autores para seleção consensual dos estudos aptos à inclusão, garantindo uma maior precisão no processo de seleção. Além disso, os artigos selecionados também serão avaliados quanto à sua qualidade metodológica por meio da ferramenta "JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies" (MOOLA et al, 2017). Após análise da qualidade metodológica dos trabalhos selecionados, os dados de interesse serão extraídos para um formulário eletrônico que será construído em uma planilha do software Excel®. Os dados serão categorizados em: características da publicação, características das amostras, características das intervenções, mensuração dos efeitos/desfechos e resultados significativos. Todos esses dados deverão ser analisados e apresentados no formato descritivo, por meio de síntese qualitativa, utilizando-se figuras e tabelas.

title: Association between impaired lung function and glaucoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis
description: Background: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. It is a chronic, progressive, age-related fibrotic disease, frequently asymptomatic at early stages and progresses gradually, resulting in significant vision loss if undetected. Observational evidence suggests that impaired lung function is potentially associated with higher risk of glaucoma. If confirmed, this association could have implications for clinical practice. However, no systematic reviews or meta-analyses have evaluated these data. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the association between impaired lung function and glaucoma and to identify the outcome measures commonly used in studies assessing lung function in relation to glaucoma risk. Methods: The review will include searches in four electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science). Primary research studies (e.g.: observational studies, randomized controlled trials) will be eligible for inclusion. Secondary research sources, as well as grey literature will be excluded. Articles entirely not in English will be excluded as the team do not have the resources to facilitate translation. Screening of titles and abstracts, and full text screening of included articles will be carried out independently by two researchers. A narrative synthesis approach will be taken to analyse the extracted data. If a group of studies with a sufficiently comparable data is identified, a meta-analysis will be performed. Quality of included studies will be assessed using risk of bias tools. Conclusions: The findings of this systematic review and meta-analysis will advance our understanding of the "lung–eye axis", through exploring the association of impaired lung function and glaucoma. Findings may potentially support biomarker discovery, highlight current gaps in research and contribute to patients' stratification for targeted glaucoma screening in high-risk groups.
keywords: Glaucoma; (Impaired) Lung Function; Fibrosis; Systematic Review; Meta-analysis
